Poetic form: Blank verse
Blank verse has a regular meter without end rhyme. English blank verse most often uses iambic pentameter: five broadly unstressed–stressed feet per line, with rhythmic variation.

Poetic form: Free verse
Free verse uses chosen rhythms and line breaks without a fixed metrical scheme. The absence of a fixed meter does not require the absence of patterned sound.
